acceptance_criteria: Structured partial worker output is returned as non-transport-error status=partial even with a nonzero process exit; focused tests cover wrapper formatting; the current stale run is recovered and labelable; AGENTS.md explicitly requires recovery plus native/local continuation after partial/error/timeout.

title: Prevent GLM worker timeout result loss

design: Patch the pinned local sub-agents-mcp 0.12.1 runtime through an idempotent postinstall script, test StreamProcessor/timeout integration behavior with Node tests, and configure a 30-minute worker ceiling with a larger outer MCP tool timeout.
acceptance_criteria: Raise internal GLM execution timeout and outer MCP timeout coherently; return accumulated Claude-compatible assistant text as a structured partial result on internal timeout; make the runtime patch survive npm reinstall; add and pass focused regression tests; obtain review-mcp review.
close_reason: Implemented durable timeout recovery, raised coordinated ceilings, passed 8 regression/integration tests, and completed review-mcp review.

title: Link discovery GC deletes sync-created external links and aborts the run (FK failure)
description: Why: probing the bookmark-to-database pipeline (2026-10-05), after syncing one danbooru post (whose declared source_url wrote a post_external_references row referencing external_links id 6363), catalog discover-links fails with FOREIGN KEY constraint failed. DiscoveryService.discover's end-of-run garbage collection (src/media_catalog/discovery/__init__.py ~99-115) deletes external_links rows that lack link_observations and external_link_references, but external_links has two more legitimate attach points it ignores: post_external_references (written by metadata sync for declared source URLs) and account_external_links. A sync-created link therefore looks like garbage to the GC, its deletion is blocked by the FK, and the entire discovery run aborts - breaking the offline workflow for any catalog that has synced metadata. What needs to be done: widen the GC predicate so a link is deletable only when nothing references it (no link_observations, no external_link_references, no post_external_references, no account_external_links); add a regression test that seeds a sync-style post_external_reference on an observation-less link and asserts discovery completes and the link survives.
close_reason: Closed

title: e621 candidate lookup rejects the e621 response envelope (malformed_response on every result)
description: Why: probing the bookmark-to-database pipeline (2026-10-05) ran catalog lookup run post:98 --provider e621 --strategy source_post_url; the request succeeded (HTTP 200) and e621 returned its normal envelope {"posts": []}, but the lookup parser expects a bare JSON list (Danbooru DAPI shape) and classified the run malformed_response with diagnostic 'lookup response is not a list' — meaning every e621 source_post_url lookup fails this way, including ones with results. Evidence retained in catalog-output/catalog.sqlite3 as candidate lookup run 4 and its raw observation payload. What needs to be done: teach the e621 lookup response parser the {posts: [...]} envelope (the e621 metadata adapter already parses this shape for post sync), add a fixture test covering both empty and non-empty e621 lookup responses, and re-run the probe seed to confirm outcome success with result_count 0.
close_reason: Closed

title: Export projections: bounded JSONL/CSV views over the evidence layer
description: Why: the 2026-10-04 gap analysis against docs/plans/raw_future_plan.md found the catalog CLI has no export surface at all (search/stats/inspection only), making the projection layer the other half of the distance to the plan's described functioning ('then projection is cheap'). All underlying evidence — raw observations, declared vs verified facts, attribution evidence per source — is already retained, so export projections are the highest-leverage non-Phase-D work toward the plan. This is the roadmap's Operations and portability thread. What needs to be done: (1) bounded JSONL/CSV export projections intended for analysis and migration, with explicitly stated projection policies — offline by default, and no private paths, credentials, cookies, signed URLs, or raw payloads in output; (2) an attribution-disagreement report: cases where two providers disagree on artist attribution, drawn from retained evidence without overriding review decisions; (3) exports carrying which source supplied each field (per-field provenance, richest observation wins per a stated policy while retaining all dissenting values); (4) later, once the Phase D relationship model exists: variant-family exports that group near-duplicates, exclude thumbnails, and prefer upstream originals. The durable database remains the evidence layer; consumer schemas and exports are projections with stated policies.

title: Artifact/work entities and typed relationship model (kernel Phase D schema half)
description: Why: the 2026-10-04 gap analysis against docs/plans/raw_future_plan.md shows the evidence backbone (observations, blobs, representations, evidence/review ledgers, storage-enforced immutability) is complete, and this is the missing layer for the plan's five-version functioning — same bytes / re-encode / crop / censored variant / edit as separately observed objects joined by evidence-backed relationships. It is the first schema consumer of the kernel epistemic vocabulary and does NOT depend on the matching research spike (tracked separately in data-processing-8nj); the halves were split on 2026-10-04. What needs to be done: (1) design the artifact/work entity — a conceptual content object that several representations and blobs manifest, designed in kernel terms; (2) one uniform typed-relationship table carrying epistemic status (observed/verified/derived/inferred/reviewed) with relationship types like same_bytes, reencoded_from, resized_from, cropped_from, censored_variant_of, edited_from, thumbnail_of, reposted_from, probably_same_work, confirmed_same_work; (3) seed it with already-deterministic or provider-observed types that need no fuzzy matching: same_bytes from existing SHA-256 dedup, thumbnail_of from occurrence variant roles, reposted_from from provider-declared source URLs; (4) leave fuzzy matcher proposals entering later as inferred candidates through the existing evidence/review ledger; (5) first projections on top, e.g. variant-family grouping that excludes thumbnails and prefers upstream originals. Constraints: new migrations must ship storage-level immutability from their first migration per the kernel spec; matching never auto-confirms identity, authorship, or same-work; keep media vocabulary (dimensions, codec, format) in the media family layer — file extension/MIME is an attribute (declared media_occurrences.mime_type vs verified assets.detected_mime_type), usable as relationship evidence, never the relationship itself; no data migration of existing tables.

title: Reviewed-target workflow: generalize library orchestration across providers and through acquisition planning
description: Why: the roadmap pipeline gap — the lower pipeline (review to metadata sync to browse to acquisition) works but requires manually translating identifiers between commands. Scope (corrected after planning recon + review, 2026-10-03): (1) extend existing target resolution (confirmed identity members and explicit stable selections already resolve offline) to report per-candidate review state and surface pending/rejected candidates as ineligible instead of silently filtering them; (2) add a "catalog library capabilities" view — provider, capability key/version, operation, adapter/schema versions, unsupported markers — offline, derived from the registry; (3) add expansion-plan-scoped acquisition planning (assets download-plan with a library-plan selector) resolving occurrence/variant selection from committed expansion associations under a fixed criteria set (variant, availability, eligibility, item limit) — browsing already keys off plans via the existing expansion-plan-id flag, so no browse surface is added; (4) complete provider-path proof: Pixiv already proven end-to-end including pause/resume — add Danbooru checkpoint/resume coverage, AIBooru execution+resume coverage, and a per-provider matrix. Terminal is a ready acquisition plan; downloads stay explicit. Tracked by OpenSpec change generalize-reviewed-target-workflow.
close_reason: Reviewed-target workflow complete 2026-10-03 (kernel Phase C): resolution reports pending/rejected account and post candidates with review state for account and post anchors; offline library capabilities view; download-plan --library-plan resolves selections from committed expansion associations under the fixed criteria set with digest parity to explicit selection; provider-path proof complete for all four capabilities (Danbooru resume, AIBooru execution+resume, 4-provider matrix). Two review passes folded in (post-anchor account candidates, digest-churn upgrade note, single-open planner evaluation, variant validation, scope-flag guard, availability/variant/reversal test coverage). Gates green; change archived as 2026-10-03-generalize-reviewed-target-workflow with specs synced.

The kernel already exists latently in the schema (platforms, raw_observations/raw_payloads, five run families, CAS assets, evidence/decision ledgers) but has no name, spec, or boundary. What needs to be done: (1) verify the kernel-to-schema mapping table in the plan against the actual migrations, per table; (2) add an OpenSpec kernel capability spec covering source and source-object identity, observation retention and revisions, the run/checkpoint contract, the evidence and review ledger, blobs, and typed relationships with epistemic status (observed/verified/derived/inferred/reviewed); (3) re-home or name module and spec boundaries where cheap, absorbing the two ready persistence follow-ups (adoption_items read into StorageWrites; single-family vocabulary colocation); (4) reconcile the observations vs raw_observations naming in the kernel vocabulary; (5) decide where the kernel spec boundary lives (standalone capability spec vs media-catalog-core sections). Constraints: no table renames, no data migration, no adapter behavior changes, no speculative abstractions without a second consumer.
notes: Task 1.2 cross-check complete (2026-10-03): walked each of the 12 provenance-kernel requirements against kernel plan section 2 mapping rows — all correspond (R1 identity<->Source/Source-object, R2 source reports, R3 provenance events, R4 blobs, R5 comparisons<->Assertion row, R6 relationships, R7 evidence, R8 review, R9 bounded runs<->Run+disciplines, R10 immutability<->discipline 1, R11 projections, R12 forward-looking). No requirement/mapping disagreements found; strict openspec validation passes.
close_reason: Architectural pass complete 2026-10-03: mapping verified against migrations 0001-0011 with corrections folded into the kernel plan; standalone provenance-kernel capability spec (12 requirements, review-corrected) synced into main specs and archived as 2026-10-03-add-provenance-kernel-spec; boundary re-homing done via beads v4i+ee0 (both closed); observations/raw_observations naming reconciled; spec boundary decided as standalone capability. description: Why: the matching spike (docs/plans/matching-spike-evidence.md, Bead data-processing-8nj) measured positives at phash@8 distance <= 10 and negatives >= 22 over 133 labeled pairs, with the catalog assets similar default conservatively at 8; the default should be revisited once the Phase D matcher proposal surface (Bead data-processing-t08 follow-on) defines its recall needs. What needs to be done: when the proposal surface is designed, decide the default --max-distance (evidence supports 10-12 where recall matters), and grow the empty same_artist_near_negative fixture class, which is the most important unmeasured false-positive source.
close_reason: Moot: the asset-similarity report this bead tuned was removed the same day at maintainer direction; thresholds are research evidence only, and any future generic matching design sets its own thresholds from fresh evidence.

title: Supervised matching research spike (kernel Phase D research half)
description: Why: before any matcher proposes fuzzy relationship types (probably_same_work, reencoded_from, resized_from), thresholds and false-positive rates must be measured evidence rather than guesses. Split from the original Phase D bead on 2026-10-04: the artifact/work and typed-relationship schema lands separately as data-processing-t08 and does not depend on this spike; conversely this spike does not block the schema work. Lower priority because it is only needed before fuzzy matchers, not before relationships exist. What needs to be done: curate a fixture set of real originals, recompressions, mirrors, and crops from the already-synced catalog; measure which signals (exact SHA-256/MD5, provider-declared vs verified hashes, perceptual hashes at multiple sizes/thresholds, aspect ratio and dimensions, chronology, source links) actually separate the classes; document distance distributions and false-positive rates; compare approaches used by czkawka-style duplicate finders per the roadmap research section, including resize and recompression robustness, crop-aware or region-based matching, and false positives among visually similar but unrelated artwork. No metric or threshold automatically establishes artist identity, authorship, same-work, source direction, or preferred quality — those conclusions require provenance and review.
notes: Session analysis 2026-10-04: this issue bundles two separable halves. (1) Schema half — artifact/work entities + the uniform typed-relationship table; seedable without any fuzzy matching via already-deterministic or provider-observed types: same_bytes (existing SHA-256 dedup), thumbnail_of (variant roles), reposted_from (source URLs). (2) Research spike — required only before matchers propose probably_same_work/inferred types. The halves can land separately. Extension/format facts are attributes (media_occurrences.mime_type declared vs assets.detected_mime_type verified), usable as evidence for reencoded_from/transcoded_from; detected-MIME vs URL-extension mismatch is cheap reviewer-facing evidence.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide multi-size perceptual hash storage
description: Why: the spike measured phash@16 (256-bit) with a wider separation margin (positives <= 36, negatives >= 114) than phash@8, but only 64-bit values are stored today. Maintainer decision 2026-10-05: hashes are identification metadata — storing an additional fingerprint size is a metadata decision (optional, cheap), not a similarity feature; it stands on its own usefulness, independent of any matching design. What needs to be done: if a concrete metadata consumer needs finer fingerprints, decide whether phash@16 is stored as a new fingerprint kind (migration plus FINGERPRINT_KINDS change) or a new algorithm version, per the kernel no-speculative-schema guardrail.

title: Comparison index for asset similarity at scale
description: Why: catalog assets similar brute-force scans all stored fingerprint pairs (O(n^2)); fine at current asset counts but the documented future split. What needs to be done: if asset counts grow into the tens of thousands, add a comparison index (BK-tree or equivalent over hex fingerprints) behind the same find_similar_pairs contract, keeping the read-only boundary and stable report shape.
close_reason: Moot: the similarity report whose scale this bead worried about was removed at maintainer direction; no product similarity surface exists.
